key_risks: Rapid Hormuz de-escalation or diplomatic resolution could reverse oil and energy gains sharply
TSMC earnings or guidance disappointment would pressure semiconductors and technology
Hotter-than-expected PPI or Warsh testimony hawkishness could lift yields and hit growth/tech
Broader risk-off from soft labor data revisions or inventory releases could compress high-beta holdings

portfolio.rationale: Direct crude exposure positioned for continued Hormuz blockade, ship attacks, and unresolved strait control that already lifted WTI/Brent to multi-week highs.
Sector leverage to elevated oil prices and geopolitical supply risk with recent price strength and positive 7d momentum.
TSMC June revenue surge and scheduled Q2 earnings conference provide near-term catalyst; Nvidia/Micron strength supports AI/chip demand.
Broad tech exposure capturing Nasdaq leadership, mega-cap AI momentum, and spillover from strong semiconductor results.
Record bank profits, markets-revenue growth, and rising consumer spending reported by major banks support near-term sector resilience.

portfolio_rationale: Concentrated on oil/energy geopolitical premium from reimposed Hormuz blockade plus semiconductor/tech catalysts from TSMC earnings and AI demand, with a smaller financials sleeve on confirmed strong bank results. Allocations target the highest-plausible one-week price drivers before July 21 close.
rationale_summary: Hormuz military developments and oil price spikes dominate short-term risk premium while TSMC results and bank earnings provide equity catalysts; portfolio overweight these over broad beta or defensive assets for the scoring window.
